material_definitions: Garnet-type Li7La3Zr2O12 (LLZO) is a solid electrolyte known for high ionic conductivity and excellent chemical stability against lithium metal.
The cubic phase of LLZO is generally synthesized through solid-state reaction and requires high-temperature sintering, such as 1230 °C.
Stabilization of the cubic phase at room temperature is typically achieved by doping with elements like Aluminum or Gallium.
The text discusses the impact of Aluminum doping (e.g., Li6.4Al0.2La3Zr2O12) on the stabilization and electrochemical properties of the garnet structure.
Reported values for bulk and total ionic conductivity serve as benchmarks for evaluating the performance of these ceramic solid electrolytes.
measurements.source_caption: Arrhenius plots of the bulk and total ionic conductivities of Li7La3Zr2O12 and related compounds.

material_definitions: This study investigates the structural and ionic conductivity properties of material series including Li3P1-xVxO4, Li3+xV1-xGexO4, and Li3+xP1-xGexO4 where x ranges from 0 to 1.
X-ray powder diffraction confirmed that the samples were phase pure and consistent with previously reported LISICON crystal structures and space groups.
The unit cell volumes of the Li3P1-xVxO4 and Li3+xP1-xGexO4 series increase with higher Ge and V content due to the larger ionic sizes of Ge4+ and V5+ compared to P5+.

Ionic conductivities were measured via electrochemical impedance spectroscopy from -30 °C to 150 °C, showing significant improvements upon aliovalent substitution that creates partial lithium occupancy.
The activation energy for conduction in these LISICON-type solid solutions ranges from approximately 0.5 eV for non-stoichiometric compositions to 1.1 eV for stoichiometric parent compounds.
